prompt: Cinematic, moody interior photography of a grand, antique library. The towering wooden shelves are packed impossibly tight with tens of thousands of books. However, a horrifying structural wrongness is immediately visible: to maximize the sheer quantity of items, every single book has been violently sliced vertically into paper-thin, millimeter-wide slivers. The shelves are overflowing with these rigid, useless fragments—just detached leather spines with no pages inside, stacked in suffocating density. A lone scholar stands in the aisle holding one of these paper-thin slices, having achieved numerical perfection but holding nothing of value. Mood: uncanny, tragic, bureaucratic dystopia, quiet wrongness. Warm, dusty library lighting contrasting with the unnatural mutilation of the objects. Photorealistic. No text, no titles on the spines, no numbers, no charts, no literal targets, no measuring instruments.
visual_logic: A library where the metric of 'total number of books' has been maximized by slicing every volume into paper-thin, unreadable fragments. The metric is mathematically perfected, but the underlying value is completely destroyed.
